英文原文:
January 18, 1903
Leonard seems to have handled the treatment 
reasonably well. No special symptoms.

March 24, 1903
After a few days his skin is covered with melanoma.
The tumors are not metastasizing very much, but 
their large number is causing a worsening in his 
general condition.

March 30, 1903
The hypersensitivity of the skin to UV radiation and 
the first lesions resulting from this are similar to 
Xeroderma Pigmentosum, an inherited illness. This 
illness is due to a mutation of the gene that protects 
against skin cancers. But, in theory, this illness is 
hereditary. 

April 18, 1903
Henceforth, Leonard will protect himself from the 
sun, but the damage is done. The light rays have 
caused an acute reaction in the Mortifilia gene inserted 
into his system. We did not foresee this, because our 
previous guinea pigs remained in their cages. At present 
the entire surface of Leonard's skin is suffering profound 
mutations.

May 25, 1903
The mutations appear to have slowed down. They are,
however, spectacular, and I ask myself how he can
survive in this condition. The wounds have transformed
into scabs that look as though they will remain, like the
bark of a tree. The damage to his skeleton and his
metabolism appear irreversible. His temporal lobes and
his upper members are the most affected parts. 

June 30, 1904
His condition has stabilized. His mental condition
concerns me as much as the appearance he has taken on,
if human appearance can still be spoken of in his case.
The only hope to cure him now is to have new guinea
pigs who have suffered in the same way, in order to test a
therapy aimed at eradicating the gene and returning the
subject to his initial condition.

September 24, 1926
This research is very long. I will not live long enough to
achieve my goal. Unless I inject myself with the treatment
and remain in the shadows until the serum is discovered.
中文译文:
1903 年 1 月 18 日
伦纳德似乎对治疗的耐受相当不错。没有特别的症状。

1903 年 3 月 24 日
几天后，他的皮肤上布满了黑色素瘤。
肿瘤的转移并不严重，但数量众多，
使他的整体状况不断恶化。

1903 年 3 月 30 日
他的皮肤对紫外线高度敏感，由此产生的初期病变
类似于着色性干皮病——一种遗传性疾病。
该病源于保护皮肤免受癌症的基因发生突变。
但理论上讲，这种病是遗传性的。

1903 年 4 月 18 日
从现在起，伦纳德会避免日晒，但损伤已经造成。
光线在他体内植入的 Mortifilia 基因中
引发了急性反应。我们事先没有预料到，
因为之前的豚鼠一直待在笼子里。目前
伦纳德全身的皮肤都在发生深度的突变。

1903 年 5 月 25 日
突变似乎已经放缓。但它们依然触目惊心，
我常常自问他如何还能活下来。伤口已经
变成看起来会永久留存的痂，如同树皮一般。
他的骨骼与代谢系统受到的损伤似乎不可逆转。
他的颞叶和上肢是受影响最严重的部位。

1904 年 6 月 30 日
他的状况稳定了下来。他的精神状态
和他如今的模样一样令我担忧——
如果他的情况还能被称作人类模样的话。
现在治愈他的唯一希望，是找到新的、
承受了同样痛苦的豚鼠，以测试一种
旨在根除该基因、让受试者恢复原状的疗法。

1926 年 9 月 24 日
这项研究太过漫长。我活不到实现目标的那一天。
除非我给自己注射这份药剂，然后隐姓埋名，
直到血清被研制出来。

Dear Leonard and Herbert,

I am writing to you as your friend.  I have just 
come out of the Seattle conference where your 
book "Eternal life is possible" had an explosive 
effect.

Your discoveries totally contradict the theories of 
Dr. Leon Korsenberg and I expect an unfavorable 
reaction from the council.  You have virulent 
detractors who fear that your research is immoral 
and casts a slur on the entire scientific community.

I have analyzed the file. Your theory certainly 
goes against the first law of medical ethics. You 
understand that without the support of a 
reputation, it will have no other destiny than 
sinking into oblivion. And, sadly, I do not have 
sufficient weight to prevent that.

You may find salvation outside the scientific 
community, you know. I fear that sanctions may 
even be taken against you and I cannot advise you 
strongly enough to locate your work in a safe place.


I remain, my dear friends, yours sincerely,

Your loyal friend, Walt Kerridan.

亲爱的伦纳德、赫伯特：

我以朋友的身份给你们写这封信。我刚从西雅图会议
回来，你们那本《永生是可能的》在会上引起了
爆炸性的反响。

你们的发现与利昂·科森伯格博士的理论完全相悖，
我预计理事会会作出不利的反应。你们有一些
激烈的反对者，他们担心你们的研究不道德，
并会给整个科学界抹黑。

我仔细分析过卷宗。你们的理论确实违背
医学伦理的第一法则。你们明白，没有声誉的
支持，它只会落得被遗忘的下场。而遗憾的是，
我没有足够的分量去阻止这一切。

你们知道，你们或许可以在科学界之外
找到出路。我担心甚至可能对你们采取制裁，
我强烈建议你们把研究成果安置到安全的地方。


亲爱的朋友们，此致

你们忠诚的朋友，沃尔特·克里丹。

英文原文:
The Mortifilia comes in the form of ciphers. 

Classification appears difficult. This endemic 
plant allows microscopic buds to appear, which do 
not appear destined to form a new plant but to 
possibly generate other leaves 
(For closer examination). 
The parasites and the spider-like appearance explain 
its capacity to propagate in an excessive manner.  
Hypothesis verified by the presence of an oversized 
sucker ensuring proliferation.

Detailed examination of the buds: the bud shows 
a stupefying germinative power. Hundreds of lines 
at the neck confirm that the species has phenomenal 
longevity. 

Cutting the xylems: the ducts are completely dry, 
no trace of humidity. How are these chlorophyll cells 
irrigated? 

The black substance released comes from glands 
located on the root; it is poisonous to its biological 
environment.  

During a darkness - light - darkness sequence, 
variations in dioxygen concentration are observed, 
whether DCPIP is present or not. The plant is 
particularly sensitive to exposure: it fears the light! 
This plant transgresses the rules of phytology. 

Molecular analyses show genetic associations 
that enable the Mortifilia to be defined as a 
non-recombinant isolat at the genetic level; 
this means that it does not have a sexual process 
for exchanging genetic material, but a parasexual 
one. I attempted an experiment during which a 
transient diploid node was formed. In this node, 
mitotic cross-over was produced at low frequency. 
The diploid node then self-haploided through the 
loss of chromosomes Using this system, two distinct 
species could exchange genetic material.  

Conclusion:

It is certain that the Mortifilia possesses abnormal 
properties.  Notwithstanding its incredible 
longevity, the plant is particularly receptive to 
crossbreeding. Research must be continued and 
the genotype of these cells must be examined 
in detail.

Type 1: Generalized melanomic attack
Prolonged exposure to UV creates micro-cancers 
in every individual, combated by the cells using 
specific proteins. The treatment stops the creation 
of these proteins. The subject therefore develops 
numerous skin cancers. These cancers revive the 
inert mutagenous properties of the treatment. The 
cancer becomes general and often gives rise to 
type 2, 3 and 4 mutations.

Very frequent, this mutation causes hypertrophy 
in the subject or hypertrophy in one of its members. 
It manifests itself in the over-development of the 
arms, of only some phalanxes, the tongue, etc. 
The hypertrophy is sometimes generalized and 
causes wounds that are often gangrenous.

The nervous system is relieved and then replaced by 
a hybrid nervous system. The symptom is spectacular, 
as the head is neglected to benefit other organs. It is 
often lost by the subject after long days left without 
bloodflow.

Type 4: merging
In a non-sterile environment, the subject sometimes 
comes into contact with foreign bodies. On occasion, 
these bodies (fly, ameba) have merged with the 
subject. The results are very variable. Sometimes 
very little of the original individual can be recognized.

OFFICE OF TECHNOLOGY OF THE CONGRESS 
Dear Sirs,

  Following the conference in Seattle, where 
your publications and particularly your work entitled 
"Eternal life is possible" were the subject of much 
discussion, the experts examined your research...
  As it was generally accepted that the use of your 
knowledge cannot be controlled, nor can the 
ecological, social and ethical consequences of your 
discoveries in the field of life be measured, we had to 
reach a decision on the maintenance, or not, of the 
research budgets.

  What safeguard can be imposed against the eugenic 
temptation foreseen by your hypotheses? Sacrificing 
the enrichment of breeding for the benefit of an 
artificial and very certainly contagious life cannot 
receive our support.

  The contribution of your work to the knowledge of 
individual characteristics is one thing, but modifying 
the transmission of these characteristics by such 
inhuman means is another.

  As a consequence, the Office of Technology of 
Congress, in agreement with the international scientific 
commission has issued a report ruling on your expulsion, 
for life, from this community. We will be required to 
legislate on the archiving or destruction of your 
research on cellular prolongation.

  In conclusion, no assistance will be allocated to you; 
your equipment and all your work will be confiscated 
and re-sold. Sworn State agents will arrive on 
8th October to seal up the premises.

  As regards Leafmore High school, a commission 
will decide on the necessity of closing it or not.

  Cordially yours.

英文原文: Pots of paint, plaster and maintenance \nproducts. Nothing interesting.
中文译文: 油漆桶、石膏和\n维修用品。没什么有趣的。

英文原文: It's closed, the lock seems to be rusted...

中文译文: 那些生物是从这边过去的。

英文原文: This glass is too dirty, I can't see \nanything through it.
中文译文: 这玻璃太脏了，\n什么都看不清。

英文原文: From here, you can see the park in front \nof the school.
中文译文: 从这里能看到\n学校前面的公园。

英文原文: That doesn't look like any animal I know.
中文译文: 这不像我认识的任何动物。

英文原文: My worst nightmare is posted up here:\nthe rules of Spanish grammar.
中文译文: 我最可怕的噩梦贴在这儿：\n西班牙语语法规则。

英文原文: Some of the teacher's things are still here,\nwhich makes me think that he was in as\nmuch of a hurry to leave as the students...
中文译文: 老师的一些东西还在这儿，\n看来他和学生们一样\n都是匆匆忙忙离开的……

英文原文: A screwdriver was lost in this room during\nthe renovation work. Please let me know\nif you find it, thank you.   Mr Garrison.
中文译文: “装修期间，这个房间里\n丢了一把螺丝刀。如果找到\n请告诉我，谢谢。加里森先生”

英文原文: It's here the teachers stored things they \nconfiscated from the students...
中文译文: 老师们没收学生的东西\n就存放在这儿……

英文原文: It's no good, I can't move it.
Maybe I'll find another wheel later.
中文译文: 也许之后我能找到另一个轮子。

英文原文: There are so many bulletin boards\nin this school...
The teachers' key box is wide open!
Maybe we can find the papers\nfor our next class exams...
中文译文: 也许能找到\n下次课堂考试的卷子……

英文原文: I hope their meals are better than what \nthe cafeteria serves us!
中文译文: 希望他们的饭菜\n比食堂给我们的好！
这学校还真是喜欢纪念品……

英文原文: The person in these two photos really looks like \nour principal when he was younger. But why \ntwo photos, is he a megalomaniac or what?
中文译文: 这两张照片里的人，真的很像\n年轻时的校长。但为什么放两张，\n他是个自恋狂还是怎样？

英文原文: Can't open it. It must be blocked by\ndebris.
中文译文: 打不开。肯定被\n残骸挡住了。

英文原文: The school computers are really old.
No, but just look at this mess!
中文译文: 不，你看看这乱七八糟的！

英文原文: A cupboard full of administration files.
I think the vending machine is out of order...
There's nothing interesting in this glass case.
中文译文: 这个玻璃柜里\n没什么有趣的。

英文原文: No point in trying, I've never seen that \ntelephone work.
中文译文: 别试了，我从没见过\n那电话能用。

英文原文: Our school won the academic basketball \ntournament three years in a row!
中文译文: 我们学校连续三年\n赢得校际篮球赛冠军！

英文原文: I think the vending machine is out of order.
These trophies, the story of our school...
中文译文: 这些奖杯，\n是我们学校的历史……

英文原文: A teacher forgot to close his locker...
中文译文: 有个老师忘了\n关他的储物柜……

英文原文: This place is really grim... Who would \nwant to come here to relieve themselves?
中文译文: 这地方真够糟的……\n谁会想来这儿方便？

英文原文: A broom and cleaning products. \nApparently, they weren't used much here.
中文译文: 扫帚和清洁用品。\n看来这儿不常打扫。

英文原文: I have 3 glasses, that should be enough.
中文译文: 我有 3 个杯子，应该够了。

英文原文: Apart from cleaning the windows, \nI don't see what use this will be to me.
中文译文: 除了擦窗户，\n我想不出这对我有什么用。

英文原文: There's really everything and anything here!
xx: Ammunition in the magazine\nyy: Team ammunition reserve\n(for this type of weapon)
中文译文: xx：弹匣中的弹药\nyy：队伍弹药储备\n（用于此类武器）

英文原文: Team ammunition reserve\n(for this type of weapon)\n
中文译文: 队伍弹药储备\n（用于此类武器）\n

英文原文: It's a bottle of acid. We can't carry it.
中文译文: 是一瓶酸液。我们带不走它。

英文原文: I filled the glass with acid.
The glass is already full of acid.
中文译文: 杯子里已经装满酸液了。

英文原文: I don't understand any of these equations.
中文译文: 这些方程式我一个都看不懂。

英文原文: This is the teacher's bench, \nthe bottles of acid are opposite it.
中文译文: 这是讲台，\n酸液瓶在它对面。

英文原文: That sucks! The cup is disintigrating!
Ah, the PC... The new plaything of spotty \npre-pubescents with glasses...
中文译文: 啊，电脑……\n戴眼镜、长痘痘的\n小屁孩们的新玩具……

英文原文: A table of arithmetic formulas... \nBrrr, that gives me the shivers!
中文译文: 一黑板算术公式……\n呃，看得我直起鸡皮疙瘩！

英文原文: Cannot connect to the Internet, \nthe server must be switched off.
中文译文: 连不上网，\n服务器肯定关着。

英文原文: There are various documents, \nbut nothing useful.
中文译文: 有一些文件，\n但没什么有用的。

英文原文: Our marks must be on these computers.
中文译文: 我们的成绩\n肯定在这些电脑里。

英文原文: I have no desire to start it up!
It's the computer that Stan worked on.
There's a completely rusty chain blocking this\ndoor. How can I speed up the process?\n
中文译文: 一条锈迹斑斑的链条锁着\n这扇门。怎么才能\n快点弄开它？

英文原文: The acid has eaten into the chain.
The acid burned through the cup.
The cup has disintigrated. It's useless.
There are lots of useless things here.
中文译文: 这里有很多没用的东西。

英文原文: It's that water that makes you ill.
中文译文: 就是这种水让人生病的。

英文原文: There's really nothing interesting in these \nglass cases.
中文译文: 这些玻璃柜里\n真的没什么有趣的。
这些电话没一个能用的……

英文原文: This fountain is not working either!

中文译文: 到处都是这些脏兮兮的饮水机！

英文原文: The next basketball match is next Saturday!\nI'll be there!
中文译文: 下一场篮球赛就在下周六！\n我一定到场！

英文原文: Hah! Is the timetable beginning to decompose?
中文译文: 哈！时刻表开始腐烂了吗？

英文原文: The Mucus in the Nose... Really the best,\nthat band!
中文译文: 鼻孔黏液……那支乐队，\n真是最棒的！

英文原文: I think it's Mr. Friedman's office...
中文译文: 我猜这是弗里德曼先生的办公室……

英文原文: I don't have the access code.
There are lots of things on the floor. \nBut I don't see anything interesting.
中文译文: 地上有很多东西。\n但没什么有趣的。
学校行政文件，\n没什么好玩的……

英文原文: An old article about our football team.\nIt was always very strong.
中文译文: 一篇关于校足球队的旧文章。\n我们队一直很强。

英文原文: A work of art... about as interesting \nas the wallpaper in this room!
中文译文: 一件艺术品……有趣程度\n和这房间的墙纸差不多！

英文原文: So this is how the filthy monsters got into the class!
中文译文: 原来那些肮脏的怪物\n是这么进教室的！

英文原文: Esto es el mapa de España, hombre!
中文译文: 这是西班牙的地图，老兄！
那画的是拉丁美洲，天哪！

英文原文: The teachers left a folder behind.\nThat proves it's not only the students who\nare scatterbrained!
中文译文: 老师们也落下了文件夹。\n看来犯迷糊的不光是学生！

英文原文: I need help to search this pipe.
中文译文: 我需要帮手才能搜查这根管子。

英文原文: This classroom could do with a good cleaning.
中文译文: 这间教室该好好打扫一下了。
那只生物把一切都砸烂了。

英文原文: It's professor Walden's satchel. \nBut what was he doing with all that stuff?
中文译文: 这是瓦尔登教授的书包。\n可他带这些东西要干什么？

英文原文:
Dear Leonard and Herbert,
I am writing to you as your friend.  
I have heard a lot spoken about you here, 
but sadly no words of praise. I have 
just left the conference in Seattle where
your book "Eternal life is possible" has
had an explosive effect.
中文译文:
亲爱的伦纳德和赫伯特：
我以朋友的身份写信给你们。  
我在这里听到不少关于你们的谈论，
但遗憾的是没有一句赞美。我刚
从西雅图开完会回来，你们的书
《永生是可能的》在那里
引起了爆炸性的反响。
弗里德曼先生的办公室

英文原文: There are two empty spaces on this map...
These are Friedman's files. If I start to \nsearch them all, I'll be at it for centuries!
中文译文: 这些是弗里德曼的文件。要全翻一遍，\n我得翻上几百年！

英文原文: The ventilation is working... \nIt's hot here, it's true...
中文译文: 通风还开着……\n这里确实挺热……

英文原文: The computer is on, like the ventilation...
It's full of trinkets of all kinds.\nHe must have traveled a lot!
中文译文: 装满了各种小玩意。\n他肯定去过很多地方！

英文原文: A post-it note from Friedman:\n"I'm in the library if you want to see me".
中文译文: 弗里德曼的便利贴：\n“想见我的话，我在图书馆”。

英文原文: I never knew it was that guy...
中文译文: 我都不知道原来是那家伙……

英文原文: We're going to hammer the Tigers!\nThey won't know what hit them!
中文译文: 我们要痛宰老虎队！\n他们连怎么输的都不知道！

英文原文: I can't wait until next Saturday!
中文译文: 我迫不及待想到下周六！

英文原文: Another filthy fountain, \nI think they want to poison us!
中文译文: 又一个脏喷泉，\n我看他们是想毒死我们！

英文原文: The last acquisitions for the library...\n
The spiral staircase is half destroyed. \nWe can't go up that way.
中文译文: 旋转楼梯塌了一半。\n这边上不去。

英文原文: There are so may books my head is spinning!

中文译文: 这是弗里德曼的办公室。

英文原文: I can't open the desk drawers,\nthey're locked.
I've never seen these tvs work.
中文译文: 我从没见过这些电视能用。

英文原文: I'm really not looking my best, am I?
中文译文: 我现在看起来真不怎么样，对吧？

英文原文: It's always this way in here...
Opening this grid won't do me any good.
中文译文: 打开这个格栅对我没什么用。

英文原文: I can understand why nobody would want to clean\nsuch filth!
中文译文: 我理解为什么没人愿意\n打扫这种脏地方！

英文原文: The neon light makes me look ill...\nunless it was that smell...
中文译文: 霓虹灯照得我一脸病容……\n也可能是那股味道……

英文原文: Esto es la foto del rey de Espana.
中文译文: 这是西班牙国王的照片。

英文原文: This closet is full of course books.
brrr...and we're like that under our skin...
中文译文: 呃……我们皮肤下面\n就长这样……

英文原文: A cell from a human body in close-up. Superb...
中文译文: 人体细胞的放大图。绝了……

英文原文: A microscope, small test-tubes...\njust like a real lab!
中文译文: 显微镜、小试管……\n真像个实验室！

英文原文: Look, a tv that's working... finally... almost...
中文译文: 看，一台能用的电视……\n终于……差不多吧……

英文原文: That's our hamster! \nHe has been experimented on a lot!
中文译文: 那是我们的仓鼠！\n它被做了好多实验！

英文原文: Those beasts have really been everywhere!
中文译文: 那些怪物真是无处不在！

英文原文: It's a long time since this room has \nseen any sunlight!
中文译文: 这房间很久\n没见过阳光了！

英文原文: Old offices, \nI wonder why they are still around...
中文译文: 旧办公室，\n不知道还留着干什么……

英文原文: If only I could be skiing right now...
中文译文: 要是现在能去滑雪就好了……

英文原文: With the tables like that, the teacher could \nsee us clearly...
中文译文: 桌子摆成这样，\n老师能把我们看得一清二楚……

英文原文: A reminder of the library rules...
You could not read them all in a lifetime.
The comic book section is not very well supplied.
Ah, all the heroic fantasy books.
I have something else to do.
These are history and geography books.
Well, they say they are memoirs written by \nour teachers.
中文译文: 据说这些是我们老师写的回忆录。

英文原文: A lot of books are missing.
Next time I am studying for the exams\nI'll know where to start.
中文译文: 下次复习考试，\n我就知道从哪儿开始了。

英文原文: This is how the creatures got in!
中文译文: 那些生物就是从这里进来的！

英文原文: It's the place we were served...things to eat.
中文译文: 这就是给我们上……吃的东西的地方。

英文原文: The menu for the week. No comment...
Oh my God! It is...actually, it was...the janitor!
中文译文: 天哪！这是……准确说，曾是……校工！

英文原文: You can see there's been a huge fight here.
中文译文: 看得出这里发生过一场恶战。

英文原文: Here's where they prepared our daily \nfood poisoning.
中文译文: 我们每天的食物中毒\n就是在这儿准备的。

英文原文: Kitchen utensils. They could have washed them...
中文译文: 厨房用具。他们本来可以洗一洗的……

英文原文: The elevator that goes to the upper floor.
The freezer, it's full of frozen meat, brrr...
Monitors and a video-recorder.\nWe can watch videos here.
中文译文: 显示器和一台录像机。\n我们可以在这儿看录像。
太好了！这台录像机能用。

英文原文: An electrical control box.\nIt can't be opened without a tool...
中文译文: 一个电气控制箱。\n没有工具打不开……

英文原文: Impossible, the control box is closed.\nI really need a tool.
中文译文: 不行，控制箱关着。\n我真的需要一件工具。

英文原文: There are even dispensers in the dining hall...
中文译文: 食堂里居然也有饮水机……

英文原文: An electrical control box.\nThe lock looks easy.
中文译文: 一个电气控制箱。\n这锁看起来很好开。

英文原文: The elevator that goes down to \nthe students' kitchen.
The freezer full of cold meat, brrr...
It appears to be simply a cupboard...
Having seen the kitchens, who'd want to \neat here!
中文译文: 看过厨房之后，\n谁还想在这儿吃饭！

英文原文: Nobody finished their plate here, too bad.
中文译文: 这儿没人吃得完自己盘里的东西，太糟了。

英文原文: The light...\nPut it back on! Quick!
I never understood anything \nabout contemporary art...
中文译文: 当代艺术我从来就\n看不懂……

英文原文: Great, I don't have a problem with my eyes!
How many times did I pretend I was sick\nto skip classes...
中文译文: 我装病逃过多少次课啊……

英文原文: Leave the drugs, time is short...
A computer, but no Internet connection...
This is the procedure to be followed in case \nof fire, earthquake, Extra-Terrestrial invasion...
中文译文: 火灾、地震、外星人入侵时\n应遵循以下程序……

英文原文: Photos of teachers during a conference...
A photo of Friedman dating from 1902...\nImpossible!
中文译文: 一张 1902 年的弗里德曼照片……\n不可能！

英文原文: It seems that this statue is as old as the school.
中文译文: 这尊雕像似乎和学校一样古老。

英文原文: It's the amphitheater reception \nthat looks over the actors' dressing room.
中文译文: 这是能俯瞰演员化妆间的\n露天剧场接待处。

英文原文: The prospectus for the next conferences...
Humano-vegetal symbiosis, \nor the art of knowing nature...

中文译文: 伟大长者的世界，与灵界沟通，有意思……

中文译文: 我才不会掀那帘子！\n这里到处是蟑螂！

中文译文: 那是我跟爸妈说的，不是跟你！

中文译文: 切……你总是这套！\n我知道你为什么不想回家！

中文译文: 我们总算摆脱了爸妈，\n你觉得我会乖乖睡在家里？

中文译文: 等等，香农！我跟你一起去！

中文译文: 我刚训练完。\n冲个澡马上就到！

中文译文: 不知道，我整晚都在\n剪我的片子……

中文译文: 从昨晚起就没人见过他……

中文译文: 好了！今天上午我们\n来讲遗传学……

中文译文: 嘿……要是他还不出现，我们 6 点在\n食堂碰头，一起去找他……

中文译文: 可警察会告诉我爸妈的！

英文原文: Pff... nothing works in this crummy school!

中文译文: 别闹了，乔什！\n现在不是玩的时候！

中文译文: 拜托，我们的调查得记录下来，\n不是吗？

英文原文: 26! I have now counted 26 cases of missing \npersons connected with the school.
中文译文: 26 个！和这所学校有关的失踪案，\n我已经数到 26 起。

英文原文: Strange that the police have never come up with \nanything about it...
中文译文: 奇怪的是，警方始终\n查不出任何线索……

中文译文: 我们学校由双胞胎兄弟\n赫伯特·弗里德曼和伦纳德·弗里德曼于 1902 年创办。

中文译文: 那说明他至少一百岁了！

英文原文: I just found their birth certificates.
中文译文: 我刚找到他们的出生证明。

英文原文: Judging by that date, they...\nHow have they stayed so young for so long?!
中文译文: 从日期来看，他们……\n他们怎么能保持年轻这么久？！

英文原文: I found this photo of a woman with \nHerbert... or Leonard.
中文译文: 我找到一张照片，一个女人\n和赫伯特……或者伦纳德在一起。

英文原文: She looks a lot like Ms. Wickson.
中文译文: 她长得很像维克森女士。

英文原文: According to this marriage certificate, Ms. Wickson \nand Leonard got married in 1885.
中文译文: 这张结婚证上写着，维克森女士\n和伦纳德于 1885 年结婚。

英文原文: Leonard was last seen in 1921. \nHe supposedly died in a plane crash,
中文译文: 伦纳德最后一次出现是 1921 年。\n据说他死于一场空难，

英文原文: but they never found his body, or even the plane...

英文原文: I found some articles about the Friedman brothers \nand their experiments,
中文译文: 我找到一些关于弗里德曼兄弟\n及其实验的文章，

英文原文: said to be so original that they "went beyond \nhuman morality".
中文译文: 据说他们的研究极其超前，\n“超越了人类道德”。

英文原文: In 1890, they went on an expedition to \nAfrica to find medicinal plants.
中文译文: 1890 年，他们远征非洲\n寻找药用植物。

英文原文: They stayed for six months and brought back a \nlarge number of hitherto unknown varieties.
中文译文: 他们在那里待了六个月，带回\n大量前所未见的物种。

英文原文: One strange specimen, Mortifilia, became \nthe basic subject of their research.
中文译文: 其中一个奇特的样本——Mortifilia，\n成了他们研究的主要对象。

英文原文: I have discovered horrible photos of disfigured \npeople in his office...
中文译文: 我在他办公室里发现了许多\n可怕的照片，照片上的人面目全非……

英文原文: I absolutely must find his lab.
中文译文: 我一定要找到他的实验室。

英文原文: Underneath the high school! In the basement!
中文译文: 就在高中下面！在地下室里！

英文原文: I managed to follow him unnoticed through the \ngardens to the basement of their house.
中文译文: 我悄悄跟着他穿过花园，\n到了他们房子的地下室。

英文原文: I searched the lab and according to Friedman's notes,
中文译文: 我搜了实验室，根据弗里德曼的笔记，

英文原文: the antiaging serum has yet to be perfected.
